title: Lab 01 — Two-Subnet Office LAN
subtitle: Junior network engineer portfolio · Cisco Packet Tracer
summary: A small office with Sales and Ops on two /26 subnets, joined by a single 2911 router. Built in Packet Tracer with IOS CLI, a security baseline, verification, and four break/fix scenarios.
imageAlt: Cisco Packet Tracer logical topology: R1 (2911) connects SW1 (Sales) and SW2 (Ops), each with two PCs.

blocks.text: A small office has two departments, Sales and Ops. Each department needs its own subnet so traffic and broadcasts stay separated. A single router connects the two subnets so the departments can still talk to each other.

items: Devices: Cisco 2911 (R1), two 2960-24TT switches (SW1, SW2), four PCs
Cabling: copper straight-through (unlike devices: PC to switch, switch to router)
No static or dynamic routing — R1 is directly connected to both subnets

blocks.text: Requirement: two equal subnets with at least 60 usable hosts each. 2^6 = 64 addresses (62 usable) → 6 host bits → /26. Mask 255.255.255.192; block size 64. Spare .128/26 and .192/26 are left unused for growth.

rows: show ip int brief on R1
Two C and two L routes
Replies (first run may drop 1–2 packets while ARP resolves)

blocks.text:
192.168.10.0/24 is variably subnetted, 4 subnets, 2 masks
C    192.168.10.0/26 is directly connected, GigabitEthernet0/0
L    192.168.10.1/32 is directly connected, GigabitEthernet0/0
C    192.168.10.64/26 is directly connected, GigabitEthernet0/1
L    192.168.10.65/32 is directly connected, GigabitEthernet0/1

rows: Ping timed out. R1 routes the request over, but PC-B2 cannot reply to another subnet without a gateway. Same-subnet pings still work.
Destination host unreachable. R1 loses its connected route to 10.64/26; show ip int brief shows administratively down. Fix: no shutdown.
Wrong mask on PC-A2 (/24 instead of /26)
With /24, PC-A2 thinks .74 is local and ARPs on LAN-A instead of using the gateway. Restore 255.255.255.192.
Unlike devices use straight-through. Packet Tracer may still bring Gi links up (Auto-MDIX); the exam still tests the cable rule.

items: Console, VTY, and enable passwords are separate — VTY needs its own password.
A switch needs a default gateway only for remote management; its ports forward on MAC address (Layer 2). The mgmt SVI exists so you can reach the switch itself.
If Sales grows to 100 hosts it needs /25 (.0–.127), which overlaps Ops' .64/26 — Ops would move to .128/26.
Router ports are off by default; no shutdown brings them up. Amber switch links are Spanning Tree settling — wait for green.

blocks.text: Open lab01.pkt in Cisco Packet Tracer to walk the same topology. Full IOS configs and the lab guide live in the GitHub repo — lab passwords are for this lab only, never production.
